segments.title: Where the letters appeared
segments.teaser: The small piece of scroll where the team reported finding letters.
segments.story: In September 2026 the Vesuvius Challenge team reported finding letters inside this scroll, and the spot they pointed to is on this little piece of papyrus. Nobody has unrolled it: what you see was revealed with X-rays and AI, on an ordinary computer.
segments.look: Look at the upper right. A row of curved strokes and a round shape stand out from the rest. Do they look like letters to you? Experts make the final call, but this is the kind of mark they look for.

segments.title: The name of the book
segments.teaser: The title of this still-rolled scroll, recovered by the team: Philodemus, On Gods, Book 8.
segments.story: Reading a title while a scroll is still rolled up is a rare thing. The Vesuvius Challenge team recovered the author and the work from this small, wide strip: Philodemus, On Gods, Book 8. The gold is their published ink map of that title region.
segments.look: Look along the strip for a row of stronger marks. This is the area scholars used to name the book; the gold is a guide, not a transcription.

segments.title: A page from the first complete scroll
segments.teaser: A wrap from the first Herculaneum scroll to be read from end to end.
segments.story: This wrap comes from PHerc. 1667, the first scroll to be virtually unrolled all the way and read by scholars as a work on ethics. The picture is the team's published ink map of one turn, so you can see what the AI sees on a scroll that has already been read.
segments.look: Look for columns and rows, the way a page is laid out. You are not being asked to transcribe it; just notice how a well-studied scroll looks in gold.

segments.title: First letters from PHerc. 211
segments.teaser: The published crop from the November 2026 announcement.
segments.story: In November 2026 the Vesuvius Challenge announced that letters had been found in PHerc. 211. This is the published crop of that area, with the team's official Reader V3 ink map. The announcement, and the expert reading, belong to the team; you can simply look at the same surface in full detail.
segments.look: Zoom until the strokes fill the screen. Switch to the original scan to see how little of this is visible without the gold.
